## Agent details

Prepared with AI assistance.

Frozen indexed samples need stable global ordering independent of the data-
parallel degree. Reuse the indexed sharding helper and add opt-in strided
ownership after global ordering, repeating before slicing so uneven epochs
remain correct. Contiguous ownership remains the default; streaming sources
retain their existing source-level sharding.

Name the policy map_dataset_dp_sharding and save it with the Grain cursor.
Reject a changed policy before restoring iterator state; historical states
without the field use contiguous ownership. DP-degree-changing checkpoint
resume remains unsupported. Document independently sharded mixture children
and preserve Grain's contiguous-shard epoch behavior.

## Verification

Owning-commit CPU checks: 144 passed in 13.70s.

Strict relevant Sphinx builds and all non-type repository hooks passed.
Three unchanged main type findings remain attributed, not reported as a clean
full type run. External reviewer and CI acceptance are separate, still pending.

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 1m 20s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/39347554712)

---
### Review of PR #5325: [data] Add global-index data-parallel ordering

- [x] Gather context (diff, related files)
- [x] Review sharding logic in `dataset.py`
- [x] Review config/types/README changes
- [x] Review tests
- [x] Post review

The core logic looks right to me. Strided mode calls `repeat()` before the `[r::W]` slice, so local index `i` on rank `r` maps to global index `i*W + r` across epoch boundaries. Grain's `ShuffleMapDataset` takes the epoch from `index // len`, so later epochs still reshuffle consistently on every rank. Pulling the two copies of the sharding code into `_shard_and_repeat` is a good cleanup. Contiguous stays the default, so existing runs and checkpoints keep their current order. Nothing below is a blocker, but #1 and #2 are worth fixing before merge.

#### 1. Name the field after what it applies to (agrees with @tianyu-l's inline comment)
`torchtitan/components/data/loader.py:78`: the option only affects map-style (indexed) graphs. `SingleDatasetConfig` with a `RandomAccessDataSource` and `DatasetConcatConfig` both go through `_shard_and_repeat`. Streaming sources reject `"strided"`. Possible names: `map_dataset_dp_sharding` or `indexed_dp_sharding`, used the same way in `DatasetIterationPolicy` and the README. The docstring could also say plainly that `"strided"` raises on streaming sources, rather than "streams use source sharding".

#### 2. Switching sharding mode on resume changes the data order without any error
`torchtitan/components/data/loader.py:166-183`: `state_dict()` saves `dp_world_size` and `load_state_dict()` rejects a mismatch, but `data_parallel_sharding` is not saved. If a run resumes with a different mode, `set_state()` still succeeds because the iterator state is just a position. The rank then reads a different set of samples, skipping some and repeating others, and nothing reports it. Since this setting decides which samples a rank owns, I suggest saving it next to `dp_world_size` and raising `ValueError` on mismatch. A missing key could be read as `"contiguous"` so old checkpoints still load.

#### 3. The PR's goal of ordering independent of DP degree doesn't cover resume yet
The motivation is "stable global ordering independent of the data-parallel degree". Strided ownership is what would let a run resume at a different DP degree, since the global position is `sum(local positions)`. However, `load_state_dict` still rejects any change to `dp_world_size`. I'd either add a `TODO(data-dp-resharding)` noting that strided mode is the starting point for that, or make the PR description and README say that only the order is DP-independent, not checkpoint resume.

#### 4. Behavior with `DatasetMixConfig`
- Map children of a mix each get strided sharding separately, and then `MapDataset.mix` combines them per rank. Interleaving the ranks does **not** rebuild a single global mixed stream. The README lists only Single/Concat, which is accurate, but a sentence saying the guarantee doesn't extend to mixes would prevent confusion.
- With `"strided"`, any mix that has a streaming child now raises. That fits "streams own their sharding", but it means the setting can't be used for mixed indexed+streaming graphs. Worth a line in the README.

#### 5. `DatasetIterationPolicy.__post_init__` (`types.py:121-125`)
- The `dp_rank`/`dp_world_size` bounds check is new behavior this feature doesn't need, which is close to the "no speculative defensive checks" guideline in CLAUDE.md. If you keep it, the error should include the actual values, e.g. `f"dp_rank={self.dp_rank} must be within [0, dp_world_size={self.dp_world_size})"`.
- The `data_parallel_sharding` value comes from user config. It would be better to validate it where the user sets it (in `GrainDataLoader.Config` or `GrainDataLoader.__init__`), and the message should include the bad value.

#### 6. A useful comment was dropped
The old `SingleDatasetConfig` code had: *"Grain preserves the epoch through sliced map indices, so the upstream shuffle uses seed + epoch on each repeat."* That's non-obvious and explains why contiguous mode can slice before `repeat()` and still reshuffle each epoch. I'd keep it in `_shard_and_repeat`'s contiguous branch, next to the strided explanation.

#### 7. README (`README.md:527-535`)
The "external indexed provider" paragraph (next-token alignment, padding, override mechanism) covers more than this PR changes, and it describes an integration this PR doesn't exercise. Consider moving it to the PR that adds such a provider, or shortening it to one sentence.

#### 8. Tests
The parametrized test covering reconstruction × shuffle × repeat × concat × DP={1,2,4} with an 11-row (non-divisible) corpus is good. Possible additions:
- A test at the `GrainDataLoader` level, so the path from `Config` to `DatasetIterationPolicy` is covered.
- A checkpoint round-trip in strided mode with `repeat=True` that crosses an epoch boundary, to confirm `get_state`/`set_state` work on the sliced, repeated dataset.
- If #2 is adopted, a test that resuming with a different mode is rejected.
- A test showing that a `DatasetConcatConfig` with a streaming child raises the "requires an indexed source" error. Right now that error fires before concat's own `TypeError`, which is fine, but nothing tests it.

#### Minor
- `_shard_and_repeat` keeps the `len(dataset) < dp_world_size` check for strided+repeat too. Strided+repeat could handle a tiny dataset, but keeping one rule for both modes is fine.

I couldn't run the unit tests or `pre-commit` here because running commands needs approval in this environment, so all of the above comes from reading the code.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** Every finding from the earlier automated review is fixed at `a99f40b`. What's left is small deletions and the PR description.

**What this PR does.** It adds `GrainDataLoader.Config.map_dataset_dp_sharding = "strided"`. With it, local row `i` on DP rank `r` of a map-style graph (Single or Concat) reads global row `i * W + r`. Repetition happens before the slice, so this still holds across epochs when the dataset length isn't divisible by `W`. The setting is saved in the loader `state_dict`, and resuming with a different setting raises an error.

**Example.** 11 rows, `W = 2`, `repeat=True`, no shuffle. Rank 1's first 4 rows:
```text
contiguous: 6 7 8 9      (its shard is rows 6..10; it starts that shard over after 10)
strided:    1 3 5 7      (row 2*i + 1; the stride carries into epoch 2, where row 11 is row 0)
resume a contiguous checkpoint with strided -> ValueError (before: rank reads different rows, no error)
```

### Earlier review, at HEAD
1. Field renamed to `map_dataset_dp_sharding`: fixed.
2. Setting saved in the checkpoint and checked on resume: fixed (`loader.py:179,196-201`).
3. `TODO(data-dp-resharding)` added, and the README says changing DP degree on resume is rejected: fixed.
4. `DatasetMixConfig` behavior documented, including the error when a child is streaming: fixed.
5. Error messages include the bad values, and the setting is validated in `GrainDataLoader.Config`: fixed. A second copy of the check is left in the policy (see below).
6. Grain epoch comment restored in the contiguous branch: fixed.
7. External-provider paragraph shortened but not removed (see below).
8. Tests added at the loader level and for resume across an epoch boundary: fixed.

### Must fix
1. PR description: it doesn't follow the `pr-description` template. There is no "Summary (human-written)" section, no concrete problem example (the "Example" above would work), and no before/after user-facing table. "External reviewer and CI acceptance are separate, still pending" isn't verification. Please also say what in-repo or planned consumer turns on `strided` (see Questions).
2. `torchtitan/components/data/types.py:109-120` -- the `map_dataset_dp_sharding` check runs twice and the policy repeats the Config default. Make the policy field required and delete its check.
3. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_grain_data.py:1148` -- `test_map_sharding_validation_at_config_and_policy` tests the existing `num_mtp_layers` check and string rejection. Delete it.

### Should consider
- `test_grain_data.py:1037` -- merge into `test_strided_map_composition_rejects_streaming_child` as a `"single"` case.
- `README.md:537-539` -- delete the external-provider paragraph; it describes an integration this PR doesn't add.

### Questions
- Which recipe or provider will set `map_dataset_dp_sharding="strided"`? The branch name suggests DSv3. If it lands in a follow-up, a link would help reviewers see why this is worth a new config field.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Strided + `repeat=True`: `dataset.repeat()` makes the length `sys.maxsize`, and `[r::W]` stays lazy. `ShuffleMapDataset` takes the epoch from `index // len`, so every rank sees the same reshuffled global order for each epoch. The loader test at `test_grain_data.py:1109` checks that rank 1's first row is 1 for strided and 6 for contiguous, and it resumes once the cursor is in epoch 2, with and without shuffle.
- `DatasetConcatConfig` passes `dp_world_size=1` to its children but keeps `strided`. Children then take the `[0::1]` path, which is the identity, so nothing changes. A streaming child now raises "requires an indexed source" before concat's `TypeError`, and a test covers it.
- Reading a missing checkpoint key as `"contiguous"` (`loader.py:196`) is correct, not a compatibility shim: every earlier checkpoint was contiguous.
- The default `contiguous` path is the same code moved into `_shard_and_repeat`, so its order and numerics don't change.
</details>

Not verified: I didn't run the CPU tests in this environment.

This is the second copy of the `map_dataset_dp_sharding` check. `GrainDataLoader.Config.__post_init__` (`loader.py:87-93`) already rejects bad values where the user sets them, and `GrainDataLoader.__init__` is the only production code that builds a `DatasetIterationPolicy`. The `= "contiguous"` default also repeats the Config default, and every other field on this internal policy is required (CLAUDE.md: "Don't give internal functions defaults that duplicate a config default").

Suggested change: make the field required (`map_dataset_dp_sharding: Literal["contiguous", "strided"]`), delete lines 116-120, and pass the value at the other constructors (`test_qwen_multimodal_data.py:86,147`, `test_chat_dataset.py:93`, and the `dataset_iteration_policy` test helper).

 For random-access training, each rank receives a contiguous slice of the globally shuffled index space, not a contiguous region of the original corpus.
 
+Set `GrainDataLoader.Config(map_dataset_dp_sharding="strided")` when each
+global index identifies one fixed sample. After global ordering, local sample
+`i` on effective-DP rank `r` reads global index `i * dp_world_size + r`:

+`DatasetConcatConfig` graphs. Streaming sources own their sharding and reject

+ranks does not reconstruct a single global mixed stream. A mix or concat
+containing a streaming child rejects strided ownership.

+Older checkpoints without this field use the historical contiguous policy.
+Global row ordering is independent of DP degree, but checkpoint resume after
+changing DP degree is not implemented and is rejected.
+
+External indexed providers can implement the existing `SourceConfig.build()`
+seam to supply a `RandomAccessDataSource`, without a storage-client dependency
+in TorchTitan. Frozen samples can use strided ownership without repacking.

 For random-access training, each rank receives a contiguous slice of the globally shuffled index space, not a contiguous region of the original corpus.
 
+Set `GrainDataLoader.Config(map_dataset_dp_sharding="strided")` when each
+global index identifies one fixed sample. After global ordering, local sample
+`i` on effective-DP rank `r` reads global index `i * dp_world_size + r`:
+
+```text
+global order:  0  1  2  3  4  5  6  7
+DP rank 0:    0     2     4     6
+DP rank 1:       1     3     5     7
+```
+
+Repetition happens before strided ownership, so interleaving the ranks still
+reconstructs the global stream when the corpus length is not divisible by DP.
+This policy applies to indexed `SingleDatasetConfig` and
+`DatasetConcatConfig` graphs. Streaming sources own their sharding and reject
+the strided policy.
+
+`DatasetMixConfig` shards its map children independently; interleaving DP
+ranks does not reconstruct a single global mixed stream. A mix or concat
+containing a streaming child rejects strided ownership.
+
+Checkpoints record the map-sharding policy and reject changing it on resume.
+Older checkpoints without this field use the historical contiguous policy.
+Global row ordering is independent of DP degree, but checkpoint resume after
+changing DP degree is not implemented and is rejected.
+
+External indexed providers can implement the existing `SourceConfig.build()`
+seam to supply a `RandomAccessDataSource`, without a storage-client dependency
+in TorchTitan. Frozen samples can use strided ownership without repacking.
+
 With effective DP greater than one, `repeat=False` is rejected because ranks can exhaust at different steps and hang training collectives. Use `repeat=True` and let the trainer's step count stop training.

+def _shard_and_repeat(
+    dataset: grain.MapDataset, policy: DatasetIterationPolicy
+) -> grain.MapDataset:
+    """Assign globally ordered indices to DP ranks and apply epoch repetition.
+
+    Strided ownership repeats before slicing so local index ``i`` on rank
+    ``r`` always reads global index ``i * dp_world_size + r``, including when
+    a corpus length is not divisible by the data-parallel degree.
+    """
+    if len(dataset) < policy.dp_world_size:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"dataset has {len(dataset)} rows, fewer than "
+            f"dp_world_size={policy.dp_world_size}"
+        )
+    if policy.map_dataset_dp_sharding == "strided":
+        if policy.repeat:
+            dataset = dataset.repeat()
+        return dataset[policy.dp_rank :: policy.dp_world_size]
+
+    shard_size, remainder = divmod(len(dataset), policy.dp_world_size)
+    shard_start = policy.dp_rank * shard_size + min(policy.dp_rank, remainder)
+    shard_stop = shard_start + shard_size + int(policy.dp_rank < remainder)
+    dataset = dataset[shard_start:shard_stop]
+    # Grain preserves the epoch through sliced map indices, so the upstream
+    # shuffle uses seed + epoch on each repeat of this contiguous shard.
+    return dataset.repeat() if policy.repeat else dataset

This is the second copy of the `map_dataset_dp_sharding` check. `GrainDataLoader.Config.__post_init__` (`loader.py:87-93`) already rejects bad values where the user sets them, and `GrainDataLoader.__init__` is the only production code that builds a `DatasetIterationPolicy`. ### Review of PR #5325: [data] Add global-index data-parallel ordering

- [x] Gather context (diff, related files)
- [x] Review sharding logic in `dataset.py`
- [x] Review config/types/README changes
- [x] Review tests
- [x] Post review

The core logic looks right to me. Strided mode calls `repeat()` before the `[r::W]` slice, so local index `i` on rank `r` maps to global index `i*W + r` across epoch boundaries. Grain's `ShuffleMapDataset` takes the epoch from `index // len`, so later epochs still reshuffle consistently on every rank. Pulling the two copies of the sharding code into `_shard_and_repeat` is a good cleanup. Contiguous stays the default, so existing runs and checkpoints keep their current order. Nothing below is a blocker, but #1 and #2 are worth fixing before merge.

#### 1. Name the field after what it applies to (agrees with @tianyu-l's inline comment)
`torchtitan/components/data/loader.py:78`: the option only affects map-style (indexed) graphs. `SingleDatasetConfig` with a `RandomAccessDataSource` and `DatasetConcatConfig` both go through `_shard_and_repeat`. Streaming sources reject `"strided"`. Possible names: `map_dataset_dp_sharding` or `indexed_dp_sharding`, used the same way in `DatasetIterationPolicy` and the README. The docstring could also say plainly that `"strided"` raises on streaming sources, rather than "streams use source sharding".

#### 2. Switching sharding mode on resume changes the data order without any error
`torchtitan/components/data/loader.py:166-183`: `state_dict()` saves `dp_world_size` and `load_state_dict()` rejects a mismatch, but `data_parallel_sharding` is not saved. If a run resumes with a different mode, `set_state()` still succeeds because the iterator state is just a position. The rank then reads a different set of samples, skipping some and repeating others, and nothing reports it. Since this setting decides which samples a rank owns, I suggest saving it next to `dp_world_size` and raising `ValueError` on mismatch. A missing key could be read as `"contiguous"` so old checkpoints still load.

#### 3. The PR's goal of ordering independent of DP degree doesn't cover resume yet
The motivation is "stable global ordering independent of the data-parallel degree". Strided ownership is what would let a run resume at a different DP degree, since the global position is `sum(local positions)`. However, `load_state_dict` still rejects any change to `dp_world_size`. I'd either add a `TODO(data-dp-resharding)` noting that strided mode is the starting point for that, or make the PR description and README say that only the order is DP-independent, not checkpoint resume.

#### 4. Behavior with `DatasetMixConfig`
- Map children of a mix each get strided sharding separately, and then `MapDataset.mix` combines them per rank. Interleaving the ranks does **not** rebuild a single global mixed stream. The README lists only Single/Concat, which is accurate, but a sentence saying the guarantee doesn't extend to mixes would prevent confusion.
- With `"strided"`, any mix that has a streaming child now raises. That fits "streams own their sharding", but it means the setting can't be used for mixed indexed+streaming graphs. Worth a line in the README.

#### 5. `DatasetIterationPolicy.__post_init__` (`types.py:121-125`)
- The `dp_rank`/`dp_world_size` bounds check is new behavior this feature doesn't need, which is close to the "no speculative defensive checks" guideline in CLAUDE.md. If you keep it, the error should include the actual values, e.g. `f"dp_rank={self.dp_rank} must be within [0, dp_world_size={self.dp_world_size})"`.
- The `data_parallel_sharding` value comes from user config. It would be better to validate it where the user sets it (in `GrainDataLoader.Config` or `GrainDataLoader.__init__`), and the message should include the bad value.

#### 6. A useful comment was dropped
The old `SingleDatasetConfig` code had: *"Grain preserves the epoch through sliced map indices, so the upstream shuffle uses seed + epoch on each repeat."* That's non-obvious and explains why contiguous mode can slice before `repeat()` and still reshuffle each epoch. I'd keep it in `_shard_and_repeat`'s contiguous branch, next to the strided explanation.

#### 7. README (`README.md:527-535`)
The "external indexed provider" paragraph (next-token alignment, padding, override mechanism) covers more than this PR changes, and it describes an integration this PR doesn't exercise. Consider moving it to the PR that adds such a provider, or shortening it to one sentence.

#### 8. Tests
The parametrized test covering reconstruction × shuffle × repeat × concat × DP={1,2,4} with an 11-row (non-divisible) corpus is good. Possible additions:
- A test at the `GrainDataLoader` level, so the path from `Config` to `DatasetIterationPolicy` is covered.
- A checkpoint round-trip in strided mode with `repeat=True` that crosses an epoch boundary, to confirm `get_state`/`set_state` work on the sliced, repeated dataset.
- If #2 is adopted, a test that resuming with a different mode is rejected.
- A test showing that a `DatasetConcatConfig` with a streaming child raises the "requires an indexed source" error. Right now that error fires before concat's own `TypeError`, which is fine, but nothing tests it.

#### Minor
- `_shard_and_repeat` keeps the `len(dataset) < dp_world_size` check for strided+repeat too. Strided+repeat could handle a tiny dataset, but keeping one rule for both modes is fine.

**Verdict: Approve -- please address the items below before merging.** Every finding from the earlier automated review is fixed at `a99f40b`. What's left is small deletions and the PR description.

**What this PR does.** It adds `GrainDataLoader.Config.map_dataset_dp_sharding = "strided"`. With it, local row `i` on DP rank `r` of a map-style graph (Single or Concat) reads global row `i * W + r`. Repetition happens before the slice, so this still holds across epochs when the dataset length isn't divisible by `W`. The setting is saved in the loader `state_dict`, and resuming with a different setting raises an error.

**Example.** 11 rows, `W = 2`, `repeat=True`, no shuffle. Rank 1's first 4 rows:
```text
contiguous: 6 7 8 9      (its shard is rows 6..10; it starts that shard over after 10)
strided:    1 3 5 7      (row 2*i + 1; the stride carries into epoch 2, where row 11 is row 0)
resume a contiguous checkpoint with strided -> ValueError (before: rank reads different rows, no error)
```

### Earlier review, at HEAD
1. Field renamed to `map_dataset_dp_sharding`: fixed.
2. Setting saved in the checkpoint and checked on resume: fixed (`loader.py:179,196-201`).
3. `TODO(data-dp-resharding)` added, and the README says changing DP degree on resume is rejected: fixed.
4. `DatasetMixConfig` behavior documented, including the error when a child is streaming: fixed.
5. Error messages include the bad values, and the setting is validated in `GrainDataLoader.Config`: fixed. A second copy of the check is left in the policy (see below).
6. Grain epoch comment restored in the contiguous branch: fixed.
7. External-provider paragraph shortened but not removed (see below).
8. Tests added at the loader level and for resume across an epoch boundary: fixed.

### Must fix
1. PR description: it doesn't follow the `pr-description` template. There is no "Summary (human-written)" section, no concrete problem example (the "Example" above would work), and no before/after user-facing table. "External reviewer and CI acceptance are separate, still pending" isn't verification. Please also say what in-repo or planned consumer turns on `strided` (see Questions).
2. `torchtitan/components/data/types.py:109-120` -- the `map_dataset_dp_sharding` check runs twice and the policy repeats the Config default. Make the policy field required and delete its check.
3. `tests/unit_tests/cpu/components/data/test_grain_data.py:1148` -- `test_map_sharding_validation_at_config_and_policy` tests the existing `num_mtp_layers` check and string rejection. Delete it.

### Should consider
- `test_grain_data.py:1037` -- merge into `test_strided_map_composition_rejects_streaming_child` as a `"single"` case.
- `README.md:537-539` -- delete the external-provider paragraph; it describes an integration this PR doesn't add.

### Questions
- Which recipe or provider will set `map_dataset_dp_sharding="strided"`? The branch name suggests DSv3. If it lands in a follow-up, a link would help reviewers see why this is worth a new config field.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Strided + `repeat=True`: `dataset.repeat()` makes the length `sys.maxsize`, and `[r::W]` stays lazy. `ShuffleMapDataset` takes the epoch from `index // len`, so every rank sees the same reshuffled global order for each epoch. The loader test at `test_grain_data.py:1109` checks that rank 1's first row is 1 for strided and 6 for contiguous, and it resumes once the cursor is in epoch 2, with and without shuffle.
- `DatasetConcatConfig` passes `dp_world_size=1` to its children but keeps `strided`. Children then take the `[0::1]` path, which is the identity, so nothing changes. A streaming child now raises "requires an indexed source" before concat's `TypeError`, and a test covers it.
- Reading a missing checkpoint key as `"contiguous"` (`loader.py:196`) is correct, not a compatibility shim: every earlier checkpoint was contiguous.
- The default `contiguous` path is the same code moved into `_shard_and_repeat`, so its order and numerics don't change.
</details>
